response: Inhaled corticosteroids (ICSs) can affect the perception of dyspnea during bronchoconstriction in asthma. Research has shown that eosinophilic inflammation of the airway wall may increase the perception of dyspnea, and the association of eosinophil counts with ICSs may result in lessening this perception. This suggests that ICSs can help reduce the severity of dyspnea experienced by asthma patients during bronchoconstriction.
